CANONICAL_NAME.value: DMTCP 3.1.2 -- Distributed MultiThreaded CheckPointing: transparent user-space checkpoint/restart of unmodified Linux processes (Cooperman, Ansel, Arya et al.)

value.lineage: Checkpoint/restart as a SURVIVAL mechanism: a coordinator signals every process in a computation; each writes its full memory image and reopens its files/sockets on restart, with no kernel module and no source change (the successor of BLCR-style and Condor-style checkpointing; used on HPC clusters). Crash-only assumption: the process may die at any instant after a checkpoint and continue from it.

value.built_to: let a long computation survive the death of its process or node by saving and restoring its entire state, without changing the program
value.pressure: node failure, preemption, job time limits on shared clusters
value.success_means: the restarted process continues exactly where the checkpoint left it

value.failure_condition: hours of computation lost at a crash; or a restart that silently diverges

cut.note: transparent distributed checkpoint/restart; a large body cut at subsystem grain -- ten mechanisms named, four plugins unread

provenance.grade_basis: Techne record nyx_handoff.where_it_came_from (populated per R34; Harmonia may re-grade)

organs.human_interpretation: all processes reach the same phase before any goes on, so the set of checkpoints is consistent
organs.mechanism: each worker sends the name of the barrier it reached; the coordinator asserts every arrival names the SAME barrier, counts arrivals, and when the count equals the number of registered peers broadcasts DMT_BARRIER_RELEASED with that name; the coordinator's view of the fleet is the min and max of per-client WorkerState (RUNNING, SUSPENDED, ..., CHECKPOINTED, RESTARTING) recomputed on every message
assumptions: one coordinator process reachable by all; peers never disagree on the next barrier name
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the consistency of a multi-process checkpoint rests here
organs.failure_landscape: UNKNOWN by run; by reading: a peer that dies mid-barrier is handled by threadIsDead on the worker side, at the coordinator by numPeers accounting (not read in full)

organs.human_name: the checkpoint thread (sleep -> suspend -> write -> resume), getcontext anchor
organs.mechanism: a dedicated thread blocks all signals but glibc's internal ones, saves its own register context ONCE (getcontext / sigsetjmp) and its stack pointer, then loops: wait for a checkpoint request from the coordinator, suspend all user threads, run pre-checkpoint hooks, save TLS and signal state, write the image, resume; on RESTART the restorer jumps back to the saved context, the originalstartup flag is false, so the thread waits for the other threads to be restored and re-enters the loop
assumptions: the thread's frame is never left, so its locals are valid targets for a jump from a different process incarnation
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the single point where 'time restarts' for the process

organs.mechanism: take the thread-list lock; loop: for each thread not the ckpt thread, by state: RUNNING -> CAS to SIGNALED and tgkill the checkpoint signal (ESRCH marks it dead); SIGNALED -> probe with signal 0 and rescan; SUSPINPROG/SUSPENDED -> count; repeat until no rescan needed; each signalled thread runs stopthisthread, saves its context and blocks on a semaphore; four documented cases of who sent the signal (comment 560-580)
organs.output: all user threads in ST_SUSPENDED with saved contexts
assumptions: a thread in a syscall will be interrupted by the signal; the wrappers make interrupted calls safe (not read)

organs.mechanism: parse /proc/self/maps into Areas; special-case nscd shared areas (remapped private), vdso/vvar, the restorer's own region; for each area write a header (address, size, prot, flags, name, offset) then the bytes; anonymous areas are scanned page-range by page-range and all-zero ranges are recorded as zero instead of written
assumptions: /proc/self/maps is complete and stable while threads are stopped

organs.mechanism: a statically linked restorer with its own syscall layer (mtcp_sys.h) reads the image header, moves itself to a reserved address range that no image area overlaps (remapMtcpRestartToReservedArea, mremap_move), switches to a new stack, unmaps every region of the current process except itself (compute_regions_to_munmap), mmaps each image area at its recorded address (mmapfile / readmemoryareas), restores brk and vdso/vvar, flushes the icache on ARM, and jumps into the checkpoint thread's saved context
assumptions: addresses in the image are still mappable (no ASLR collision; vdso relocation handled 624-760)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the only code that runs while the process is 'nobody' -- it cannot use libc
organs.failure_landscape: UNKNOWN by run; by reading: an image area overlapping the restorer or the vdso is the designed failure surface (doAreasOverlap, validateRestoreBufferLocation)

organs.mechanism: dmtcp_launch sets LD_PRELOAD to the plugin libraries plus libdmtcp.so; each wrapped libc/syscall function is redefined; the real one is looked up once (dlsym RTLD_NEXT style, syscallsreal.c initialize_libc_wrappers) into a table; a wrapper takes the DMTCP lock, translates ids, records fds/sockets/pids, calls _real_X, and dispatches plugin events
organs.input: every wrapped call from the application
organs.output: the same call, observed and translated
assumptions: the application is dynamically linked and does not bypass libc (record: dmtcp_nocheckpoint / static binaries are the known hole)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: transparency: the application is never modified

organs.mechanism: a template table virtual<->real with updateMapping; the application only ever sees virtual pids/tids/ipc ids (the wrappers translate both ways); after restart, when the kernel hands out new real ids, the table is updated and the application's ids stay valid
organs.input: real ids from the kernel; virtual ids from the application
assumptions: every path by which an id can reach the application is wrapped

organs.mechanism: before the snapshot, for every TCP connection to another checkpointed process: send a magic cookie string through the socket and read from it until the cookie arrives, storing everything read (the in-kernel bytes now live in user memory, which the image captures); send buffers are scaled to make room; after resume/restart refillAllSockets writes the stored bytes back; sockets to external processes are not drained (577)
assumptions: both ends are under DMTCP so the cookie is consumed, never delivered to the application
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: state the process does not own is pulled inside the process boundary

organs.mechanism: after restart each side opens a restore socket, registers its incoming/outgoing connection identifiers and address with the coordinator's key-value service (registerNSData / sendQueries), learns the peer's new address, reconnects, and the old fd is dup'd onto the new socket (doReconnect)

the checkpoint cycle emits a fixed vocabulary of events (INIT, PRECHECKPOINT, RESUME, RESTART, CLOSE_FD, DUP_FD, VFORK_*...); each plugin switches on them (socketconnlist.cpp 27-70); the pluginmanager calls them in registration order -- not read

pressures.condition: work runs for hours on machines that fail or are reclaimed; the program has no save/restore of its own and cannot be modified
pressures.failure_condition: hours lost at a crash; or a restart that silently diverges (record)
pressures.world_punishes: recomputation from zero; divergence after restore
pressures.world_rewards: capturing all state that determines the future and reinstating it exactly
pressures.observable_consequence: the record's oracle: a counter resumes at the checkpointed value, not zero
pressures.vacuity_condition: no failures; or programs that already checkpoint themselves
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: rerun from the start (correct, pays the full cost); the world must charge for lost work
pressures.cheat_control: a program that persists its own counter to a file must pass the oracle without DMTCP; if the world rewards it equally, the world measures persistence, not transparency
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: fault tolerance for unmodified programs

pressures.condition: identifiers the program holds (pids, tids, fds, addresses, ports) are assigned by the OS and differ in the new incarnation while the program's memory still holds the old ones
pressures.resource_or_constraint: OS naming is not under the program's control
pressures.failure_condition: a restored program signals the wrong pid, writes to a closed fd, connects to a dead address
pressures.world_rewards: an indirection layer that owns the names the program sees and remaps them
pressures.vacuity_condition: an OS that preserves ids across restart (none does)
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: never use ids (impossible for real programs)
pressures.cheat_control: a program that only ever uses names DMTCP virtualises must restart cleanly; one that smuggles a raw pid through shared memory must fail -- the world can tell

pressures.condition: bytes in flight live in the kernel (socket buffers) and in peers, invisible to a memory image
pressures.resource_or_constraint: the process boundary is narrower than the computation's state
pressures.failure_condition: a restart that loses or duplicates in-flight messages
pressures.world_rewards: a protocol that flushes external state into the process (cookie-drain) and replays it after
pressures.observable_consequence: message counts before and after restart
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: quiesce the whole application first (needs cooperation the pressure forbids)
pressures.cheat_control: a pair of processes given a shared flush-and-replay must show byte-identical streams across restart

pressures.condition: a checkpoint of a distributed computation is only useful if no message is recorded as received but not sent; processes have no shared clock
pressures.world_rewards: a barrier protocol (a coordinator counting arrivals, or its distributed equivalent)
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: stop the world by an external signal (works if all processes are on one host)
pressures.cheat_control: a fleet with a known-consistent cut injected must restart cleanly; a fleet snapshotted at random times must sometimes fail -- if it never does, the world is not exercising the pressure
